messages.author: c7843a9d9b559ffc
messages.subject: read.cross removing genotype data
parts:
I seem to have a problem with the read.cross command in R/qtl removing
SNP genotype data on the X chromosome that it doesn't like. The
removed genotypes appear to possibly be the result of
double-recombination events in both gametes (ie: F2 intercross female X
chromosome genotypes: B A A A A A A A A A A B B B B B, where B=BB,
A=AA, and H=AB or BA). This also happens in the F3 progeny from the
same cross if there are apparent double-recombination events in one or
both gametes (ie: F3 intercross female X chromosome genotypes: B B B A
A H H H H H H H H H H H). Am I simply setting up the pgm column wrong
on the data, or is there some other explanation for the data removal?
Is there a way to prevent R/qtl from removing this data?

Thanks,
Gloria

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: read.cross removing genotype data
parts:
Dear Gloria,

In your F2 data, there is one individual indicated to be a female but
having
genotype data that indicates a male (only A's and B's). Reading in the
data, I get the warning message "Omitting 10 AA genotypes from females
from cross (BxA)x(BxA) on the X chr." Those are all from that one
individual.
It drops those A genotypes, but probably it's better to check the sex
of the
individual and either fix that or drop the individual.

Unfortunately, your F3 data is problematic for R/qtl. We don't
really have
facilities for analyzing genotype data from an F2. The autosomal
data might
be treated as an F2 with an expanded map, but the X chromosome data
doesn't
fit our scheme. We're just not set up to deal with an F3.

Regards,
karl
